## Hook (first 3 seconds)
**On-screen text:** "Your grinder is ruining your coffee"
**Visual:** Tight shot of a blade grinder spinning, then a sudden cut to the result — a pile of grounds that's half dust, half gravel.
**VO:** "If you use a blade grinder, you're not grinding coffee — you're smashing it."

*(Negative-framing hook. One loop: what's wrong with the grounds, and what it costs you.)*

## Body (3-4 scenes with cues)

**Scene 1 — The problem, shown (≈4s)**
**Visual:** Close-up pour of blade-ground coffee onto a white plate. Spread it with a finger — big chunks next to fine powder.
**On-screen text:** "Blades chop at random"
**VO:** "A blade just chops whatever's in its path. You get boulders and dust in the same batch."

**Scene 2 — Why it wrecks the cup (≈5s)**
**Visual:** Split screen — dust side labelled "over-extracted / bitter," boulder side labelled "under-extracted / sour."
**On-screen text:** "One grind, two bad flavours"
**VO:** "Water rips flavour out of the dust too fast and barely touches the chunks. So you taste bitter and sour at once."

**Scene 3 — The fix (≈5s)**
**Visual:** Burr grinder turning; grounds falling onto the same white plate — uniform, even.
**On-screen text:** "Burrs grind to one size"
**VO:** "A burr grinder crushes every bean to the same size. Even grounds, even extraction, a cup that actually tastes like it should."

## CTA
**Visual:** Back to the two plates side by side — ragged vs. even.
**On-screen text:** "Burr, not blade."
**VO:** "Know someone still running a blade grinder? Send them this before they make another pot."

*(One ask, reshape-oriented for Shorts — points to a specific person rather than engagement bait. Payoff lands on the even grounds before the ask.)*
